title: PeopleOS statutory dataset 2026.10
notice: Current statutory values for the launch jurisdictions, researched against official sources on the date shown. They are configuration data, loaded pending and activated by a second operator; every value is versioned and replaced by a new version when the law changes. Loading them is not a claim of legal compliance: Markedge's tax advisers remain responsible for its treatment (decisions B-8, B-9). Values marked pending_verification cannot be used until an operator verifies them with a reference.

jurisdictions.IN: India GST: supplier side (domestic and export).
jurisdictions.EU: EU VAT: destination side, one rule per member state (27).
jurisdictions.US: US sales tax: destination side, one rule per state. Researched: California (two versions), Texas, New York, Washington, Pennsylvania. Every other state and the District of Columbia: PENDING_VERIFICATION (no rule; invoices to them are refused).

tax_rules.summary: India GST on PeopleOS (IT / online services): 18 % (CGST 9 + SGST/UTGST 9, or IGST 18); export of services zero-rated under LUT when the export conditions are met

intra_state.description: Supplier and place of supply in the same State: CGST (CGST Act s.9(1)) + SGST, 9 % each (Notification 11/2017-CT(R) S.No. 21(ii) as amended by 15/2025-CT(R)).

intra_union_territory.description: Same Union territory without legislature (UTGST Act s.2(8): Andaman & Nicobar, Lakshadweep, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu, Ladakh, Chandigarh): CGST + UTGST (UTGST Act s.7(1)), 9 % each.

inter_state.description: Different States/UTs: IGST (IGST Act s.5(1), s.7(3)), 18 % (Notification 8/2017-IT(R) as amended by 15/2025-IT(R)).

export_of_services.wording: SUPPLY MEANT FOR EXPORT/SUPPLY TO SEZ UNIT OR SEZ DEVELOPER FOR AUTHORISED OPERATIONS UNDER BOND OR LETTER OF UNDERTAKING WITHOUT PAYMENT OF INTEGRATED TAX
export_of_services.description: Export of services (IGST Act s.2(6)): supplier in India, recipient outside India, place of supply outside India (s.13(2)/(12): recipient's location), payment in convertible foreign exchange, not a distinct person; zero-rated (s.16(1)(a)) and supplied under a Letter of Undertaking without payment of IGST (s.16(3), CGST Rules r.96A, LUT in FORM GST RFD-11 valid for the financial year). Invoice wording: CGST Rules r.46 proviso (form in force since 01.11.2024).

tax_rules.source: CBIC / GST Council
tax_rules.source_reference: Notification No. 11/2017-Central Tax (Rate) S.No. 21(ii), as amended by No. 15/2025-Central Tax (Rate) dated 17.09.2025 (w.e.f. 22.09.2025); IGST Notification No. 8/2017-Integrated Tax (Rate), amended by 15/2025-Integrated Tax (Rate); CGST Act s.9; IGST Act ss.2(6), 5, 7, 8, 12, 13, 16; UTGST Act s.7; CGST Rules rr.34(2), 46, 96A

verification.method: Rates read in the notification texts on the CBIC portal (no later amendment found through 30.09.2026); Act and Rule sections read on CBIC's consolidated pages.

statutory_notes.place_of_supply: Both in India: IGST Act s.12(2) (registered recipient: its location; unregistered: address on record, else supplier's location). Cross-border: s.13(2) location of the recipient; online information and database access or retrieval services (OIDAR, s.2(17) as widened from 01.10.2023, which lists cloud services) s.13(12), also the recipient's location.
statutory_notes.zero_rating: s.16(1)(a). Two routes: under LUT/bond without IGST (s.16(3), r.96A) — configured here; or with IGST and refund (s.16(4), Notification 01/2023-IT as amended by 05/2023-IT: all services) — not configured.
statutory_notes.export_conditions_evaluated: recipient outside India; invoice in a foreign currency (payment in convertible foreign exchange; INR where permitted by the RBI is not configured); a valid IN_LUT registration on the supplier profile; customer not recorded as an establishment of the supplier; the value reported in INR.
statutory_notes.reporting_value: CGST Rules r.34(2): the rate of exchange for taxable services is the rate determined under generally accepted accounting principles for the date of time of supply.
statutory_notes.classification: The SAC of PeopleOS is a judgement to be confirmed by Markedge's GST adviser (no CBIC circular classifies SaaS). Candidates, all at 18 %: 998314 IT design and development services; 998315 Hosting and IT infrastructure provisioning services; 997331 Licensing services for the right to use computer software and databases; 998431/998439 on-line content. Notification 78/2020-CT: 4-digit SAC up to Rs 5 crore turnover, 6 digits above. Invoices cannot be issued until the SAC is recorded in a new version of this rule.
statutory_notes.rounding: Each tax amount is rounded once per line to the paisa, half up (a configuration choice; CGST Act s.170 rounds amounts payable to the nearest rupee).
statutory_notes.not_configured: SEZ supplies, UIN holders, the export-with-payment route, INR export receipts permitted by the RBI.

tax_rules.summary: UK VAT on services from abroad: business customers account for VAT (reverse charge); consumers: 20 % due from a UK-registered supplier

b2b_reverse_charge.description: B2B general rule: supplied where the customer belongs (VATA 1994 s.7A(2)(a); VAT Notice 741A para 6.3); the UK business customer accounts for the VAT (s.8; Notice 741A para 5.6); the amount payable excludes UK VAT (para 5.12). Evidence: the customer's VAT number (para 2.4); HMRC also accepts other commercial evidence (para 6.3), which PeopleOS does not record, so a VAT number is required here.

b2c_digital_services.description: Digital services to UK consumers: supplied where the consumer belongs; a supplier based outside the UK must register for UK VAT, with no threshold (HMRC digital services guidance; Notice 741A para 2.6; Notice 700/1 para 9.3). Standard rate 20 % since 4 January 2011.

tax_rules.source: HMRC / GOV.UK
tax_rules.source_reference: VAT rates (standard rate 20 % from 4 Jan 2011); VATA 1994 ss.7A, 8 (as reproduced in HMRC manual VATPOSS06200, VATPOSS14200); VAT Notice 741A paras 2.4, 2.6, 5.6, 5.12, 6.3; VAT rules for supplies of digital services to consumers

verification.method: GOV.UK pages and HMRC manuals read; legislation.gov.uk could not be opened (bot challenge), the statute text was read as reproduced by HMRC.

statutory_notes.place_of_supply: B2B: where the customer belongs (s.7A(2)(a)); B2C: where the supplier belongs, except digital services to consumers (where the consumer belongs).
statutory_notes.reverse_charge: The UK business customer accounts for VAT; an overseas supplier making only reverse-charge supplies is not entitled to register (Notice 741A para 2.6).
statutory_notes.invoice_wording: HMRC prescribes no wording for an invoice from a supplier outside the UK; none is configured.
statutory_notes.evidence: VAT number presumption (para 2.4); without a VAT number or other evidence, treat as B2C (para 6.3; digital services guidance).
statutory_notes.use_and_enjoyment: Electronically supplied services B2B may be subject to use-and-enjoyment adjustments (Notice 741A s.13) — not configured.

tax_rules.summary: UAE VAT on electronic services from a non-resident: a VAT-registered recipient accounts for VAT (reverse charge); otherwise 5 % due from a UAE-registered supplier

b2b_reverse_charge.description: Place of supply in the UAE (Decree-Law Art. 30(2) B2B; Art. 31 electronic services: where used and enjoyed); a VAT-registered recipient receiving services from a non-resident who does not charge VAT accounts for it (Art. 48; Executive Regulation Art. 48(3), (5)(a)); self-invoicing removed for imports from 1 January 2026 (FDL No. 16 of 2025; FTA VATP046).

unregistered_recipient.description: No registered recipient to account for the tax: a non-resident must register regardless of the threshold (Decree-Law Art. 13(2); Executive Regulation Art. 7(6)) and charge the standard rate of 5 % (Art. 3).

tax_rules.source: Federal Tax Authority (UAE)
tax_rules.source_reference: Federal Decree-Law No. 8 of 2017 on VAT (consolidated to FDL 16/2024) Arts. 3, 13, 30, 31, 45, 48, 85; Executive Regulation (Cabinet Decision 52/2017, consolidated to Cabinet Decision 149/2026) Arts. 7, 8, 23, 31, 48; FDL No. 16 of 2025 (from 1 Jan 2026); FTA public clarification VATP046

verification.method: FTA consolidated English texts read (each marked 'not an official translation'; the Arabic text is binding); the amended wording of Art. 48(1) after FDL 16/2025 was not obtained.

statutory_notes.electronic_services: Executive Regulation Art. 23(2): services automatically delivered over the internet, including the supply and updating of software. Treating PeopleOS as an electronic service is an interpretation (no FTA ruling found).
statutory_notes.zero_rating_and_export: Supplier side (a UAE supplier): exports of services are zero-rated (Decree-Law Art. 45(1); Executive Regulation Art. 31(1)(a): recipient without residence in an Implementing State and outside the State). Not applicable to Markedge's Indian entity; recorded for completeness.
statutory_notes.registration: Non-residents: Art. 13(2), no threshold where no other person is obliged to pay the tax. Residents: mandatory AED 375,000 (Executive Regulation Art. 7(1)); voluntary AED 187,500 (Art. 8(1)).
statutory_notes.unregistered_business: A UAE business customer without a TRN cannot account under Art. 48 (which applies to a Taxable Person): treated like any unregistered recipient (supplier registration required). Adviser to confirm.
statutory_notes.trn: 15 characters on the FTA verification form (no official statement of the format found).

tax_rules.summary: Belgium: business customers with a VAT number account for VAT (reverse charge); consumers: 21 % due from a registered supplier (non-Union OSS)

b2b_reverse_charge.description: Place of supply: the customer's establishment in Belgium (Directive 2006/112/EC Art. 44); VAT payable by the customer as the supplier is not established there (Art. 196). Evidence: a VAT identification number validated through VIES (Regulation 282/2011 Art. 18(1); Regulation 904/2010 Art. 31); for electronically supplied services a customer without a VAT number may be treated as a non-taxable person (Art. 18(2)). Invoice mention 'Reverse charge' (Art. 226(11a)).

b2c_electronic_services.description: Electronically supplied services to a consumer in Belgium: supplied where the customer resides (Art. 58(1)(c); Annex II; Regulation 282/2011 Art. 7). A supplier not established in the EU accounts for Belgium's VAT (21 % standard) through the non-Union scheme (Arts. 358a, 359) from the first euro (the EUR 10,000 threshold of Art. 59c applies only to suppliers established in one member state).

statutory_notes.b2b: No VAT charged by a non-EU supplier; the customer accounts for it at its member state's rate.
statutory_notes.classification: SaaS is treated as an electronically supplied service under Regulation 282/2011 Art. 7(1) (an application of the test, not an explicit rule).

Evidence: a VAT identification number validated through VIES (Regulation 282/2011 Art. 18(1); Regulation 904/2010 Art. 31); for electronically supplied services a customer without a VAT number may be treated as a non-taxable person (Art. 18(2)). Invoice mention 'Reverse charge' (Art. 226(11a)).

b2c_electronic_services.description: Electronically supplied services to a consumer in Sweden: supplied where the customer resides (Art. 58(1)(c); Annex II; Regulation 282/2011 Art. 7). A supplier not established in the EU accounts for Sweden's VAT (25 % standard) through the non-Union scheme (Arts. 358a, 359) from the first euro (the EUR 10,000 threshold of Art. 59c applies only to suppliers established in one member state).

tax_rules.source: European Commission — Taxes in Europe Database (TEDB)
tax_rules.source_reference: TEDB standard rate, retrieved 2026-10-08; Directive 2006/112/EC (consolidated 14.04.2025) Arts. 44, 58, 59c, 196, 226(11a), 358a, 359, Annex II; Implementing Regulation (EU) 282/2011 Arts. 7, 18

verification.method: Standard rate read from the European Commission's TEDB. Directive and Regulation articles read in the consolidated texts.

statutory_notes.effective_from: unchanged in every TEDB snapshot since 1 January 2024 (its earlier start date is not recorded here)
statutory_notes.b2b: No VAT charged by a non-EU supplier; the customer accounts for it at its member state's rate.
statutory_notes.classification: SaaS is treated as an electronically supplied service under Regulation 282/2011 Art. 7(1) (an application of the test, not an explicit rule).

tax_rules.summary: California: SaaS not taxable until 31 December 2026

saas.description: Not taxable: a prewritten program transferred by remote telecommunications, the purchaser obtaining no tangible personal property (Regulation 1502(f)(1)(D)). Ends 31 December 2026 (SB 122).

tax_rules.source: California Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA)
tax_rules.source_reference: Sales and Use Tax Regulation 1502(f)(1)(D), (c)(7)

verification.method: Official state tax authority pages and statutes read.

statutory_notes.effective_from: in force on 2026-10-08 (earlier start not recorded)
statutory_notes.economic_nexus: over $500,000 of sales for delivery in California in the current or preceding calendar year (R&TC s.6203(c)(4)), no transaction count
statutory_notes.purchaser_use_tax: none today (SaaS is not tangible personal property until 2027)

tax_rules.summary: California: SaaS taxable from 1 January 2027 (7.25 % + district taxes)

saas.description: Taxable from 1 January 2027: digital products, including prewritten SaaS accessed remotely, become tangible personal property (SB 122, Stats. 2026 ch. 23; CDTFA Special Notice L-1036). Statewide rate 7.25 % plus district taxes (0.10 %–2.00 %) by the customer's address; sourced to the customer's (billing) address.

tax_rules.source: California Department of Tax and Fee Administration (CDTFA)
tax_rules.source_reference: SB 122 (Stats. 2026, ch. 23); CDTFA Special Notice L-1036 (September 2026); CDTFA sales and use tax rates; R&TC s.6203(c)(4)

verification.method: Official state tax authority pages and statutes read.

statutory_notes.economic_nexus: over $500,000 (R&TC s.6203(c)(4)); SaaS sales count once digital products are tangible personal property (an inference)
statutory_notes.large_buyer: over $5,000,000 of digital products to one purchaser in 2027 may shift liability to the purchaser (use tax direct payment permit)
statutory_notes.local_rates: district taxes vary by address (CDTFA 'Find a Sales and Use Tax Rate by Address'): not configured
statutory_notes.purchaser_use_tax: purchaser reports use tax when the seller does not collect (from 2027)

tax_rules.summary: Texas: SaaS taxable as data processing, 6.25 % on 80 % of the price + local

saas.description: SaaS is a data processing service (Publication 96-259; Tax Code s.151.0035; Rule 3.330), taxable at 6.25 % (s.151.051(b)) on 80 % of the charge (20 % exempt, s.151.351), plus local taxes up to 2 % (or the 1.75 % single local use tax rate a remote seller may elect, Rule 3.334).

tax_rules.source: Texas Comptroller of Public Accounts

verification.method: Official state tax authority pages and statutes read.

statutory_notes.effective_from: in force on 2026-10-08 (the 80 % rule since 1 October 1999)
statutory_notes.economic_nexus: total Texas revenue of $500,000 or more in the preceding twelve months (Rule 3.286), no transaction count, effective 1 October 2019
statutory_notes.local_rates: up to 2 % by location (Sales Tax Rate Locator) or the 1.75 % single local use tax rate (Rule 3.334): not configured
statutory_notes.purchaser_use_tax: Texas purchasers owe use tax when the seller does not charge Texas tax

tax_rules.summary: New York: SaaS taxable, 4 % + local

saas.description: Remote access to prewritten software is taxable (TB-ST-128; Tax Law ss.1101(b)(6), (14), 1115(o)): state rate 4 % plus local city, county or school district taxes (and 0.375 % in the MCTD), sourced to where the purchaser uses or directs the use of the software.

tax_rules.source: New York State Department of Taxation and Finance
tax_rules.source_reference: Tax Bulletin TB-ST-128 (updated 31 March 2026); Tax Law ss.1101(b)(6), 1101(b)(14), 1115(a)(28), 1115(o); Publication 718

verification.method: Official state tax authority pages and statutes read.

statutory_notes.effective_from: in force on 2026-10-08 (earlier start not recorded)
statutory_notes.economic_nexus: over $500,000 of receipts AND more than 100 sales into New York in the preceding four sales tax quarters, effective 21 June 2018
statutory_notes.multi_location_users: tax applies to the share of the price for users in New York
statutory_notes.local_rates: by jurisdiction (Jurisdiction/Rate Lookup by Address): not configured
statutory_notes.purchaser_use_tax: purchasers file use tax (Form ST-130) when sales tax is not paid

tax_rules.summary: Washington: SaaS taxable, 6.5 % + local

saas.description: Remote access software is a retail sale (RCW 82.04.050(6)(b)(i); WAC 458-20-15503) subject to retail sales tax: state rate 6.5 % plus local rates by location. ESSB 5814 (from 1 October 2025) also taxes IT services such as implementation and training.

tax_rules.source: Washington State Department of Revenue

verification.method: Official state tax authority pages and statutes read.

statutory_notes.effective_from: in force on 2026-10-08 (earlier start not recorded)
statutory_notes.economic_nexus: over $100,000 of gross receipts sourced to Washington in the current or prior calendar year (from 1 January 2020), no transaction count; retailing B&O tax also applies (not configured)
statutory_notes.multiple_points_of_use: business buyers using the software in and outside Washington may give an exemption certificate and self-assess (RCW 82.08.0208(4))
statutory_notes.local_rates: by location (Tax Rate Lookup Tool): not configured
statutory_notes.purchaser_use_tax: businesses report use tax on their excise return

tax_rules.summary: Pennsylvania: SaaS taxable, 6 % (+ Allegheny 1 %, Philadelphia 2 %)

saas.description: Canned software accessed through a SaaS agreement is taxable when the user is in Pennsylvania (72 P.S. s.7201(k)(1), (m)(2), Act 84 of 2016): state rate 6 %, plus 1 % in Allegheny County and 2 % in Philadelphia; a Pennsylvania billing address presumes all users are in Pennsylvania.

tax_rules.source: Pennsylvania Department of Revenue

verification.method: Official state tax authority pages and statutes read.

statutory_notes.effective_from: in force on 2026-10-08 (the Act 84 start date is not stated on the official page)
statutory_notes.economic_nexus: Pennsylvania annual gross sales greater than $100,000 in the prior year (from 1 July 2019), no transaction count
statutory_notes.local_rates: Allegheny County 1 %, Philadelphia 2 %: locality not configured
statutory_notes.purchaser_use_tax: use tax at the sales tax rate when no sales tax is paid to a vendor
